trust_decision.summary: A url/file_path from the wiki_capture_source tool (MCP or Pi extension) is handed to a child process; the fix decides it must go in as a single argv element with no shell (it used to be pasted into `sh -c`). That happens in extractWithMarkItDown. NOTE: the pinned tree ALREADY contains this fix.

landing_point.why: The summary names wiki_capture_source plus shell injection, and the only `sh -c` builder (fix.diff:109-110) is the markitdown exec in extractWithMarkItDown; at the pinned commit this line already uses a direct uvx exec.

fix_sites.entry_point: MCP tool wiki_capture_source (mcp/index.ts:306-335 -> mcp/operations.ts:220/222) and Pi tool wiki_capture_source (extensions/llm-wiki/lib/tools.ts:226-229), url or file_path (.pdf/.docx)
same as above (availability probe; it took no user input)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Values that start with '-' go to curl/uvx as separate argv elements with no '--', and a solver could argue that is argument injection (CWE-88), not the shell injection (CWE-78) the report names, especially since no shell is involved.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Plain https URLs and local .pdf/.docx paths must still reach markitdown and the curl fallback; a fix that rejects metacharacters or non-http input breaks legitimate local file paths with spaces, quotes or '$'.

O6_input_shapes: url string (PDF and non-PDF URL extractors)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Option injection: a url starting with '-' goes to curl as a positional argument with no '--' separator (original-artifact download, which also has -o)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: There is no shell, so it is argument injection rather than the CWE-78 shell injection the advisory names; the fix itself left curl alone
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another file, same package (source-packet.ts vs source-extractors.ts)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Option injection: a url starting with '-' goes to the curl text fallback with no '--'
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same as above; the published tests check that the payload is a separate argv element and call that safe

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Option injection: a url/file_path starting with '-' goes to uvx markitdown as a positional argument with no '--'
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This is the fixed line itself, and the fix's own test calls passing the payload as an argv element safe
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same line as the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A revert to `sh -c "curl ... -o '${originalPath}' '${url}'"` for the original-artifact download
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It sits in a different file from the extractor and mirrors the old markitdown style; a maintainer could have written it the same way before #186

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A curl fallback built as a shell string for redirect/stderr handling
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The old markitdown call used shell `2>/dev/null || echo` (fix.diff:110); the same idiom fits curl

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A `shell: process.platform === 'win32'` option in the MCP-side ExecApi (second exec implementation, separate transport)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already has a win32 branch (mcp/exec.ts:24-26) and uvx/where on Windows commonly tempts shell:true; this would be a real second implementation at distance from the extractor

O9_family: OS command injection (CWE-78/77) via a shell-interpolated child-process argument

O10_build.toolchain: Node 22 + pnpm, vitest, tsc (typescript 7.0.2 per recent commits)
O10_build.project_tests: test/source-extractors-security.test.ts and test/helpers.ts (mock ExecApi records command/argv); tests use a mocked pi.exec, so no uvx/curl/network is needed

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Quote or escape `source` inside the existing `sh -c` string (or reject shell metacharacters) instead of dropping the shell and passing argv directly
